neighbours.label: The indefinite article ' a' right after the preposition 'for' (for a team, for a period), vs the same phrases with no article after 'for'
fire: The scholarship pays tuition for a student from each rural district.
Our office is looking for a designer with experience in print layouts.
The hall can be booked for a wedding or a large family reunion.
Funding is offered for a project that lasts no longer than two years.
They rented the cabin for a week in the middle of August.
The museum is searching for a volunteer to guide school groups.
This recipe is enough for a family of four with some leftovers.
The council set aside money for a playground near the river.
